scope: Distinct named GDI32.dll imports in PE files under test/binaries.

handlerCoverage.meaning: Every named corpus import reaches a WAT handler without crash_unimplemented. This is a dispatchability gate; the partial-fidelity contracts below remain explicit and are not counted as complete semantics.

metafile: CreateMetaFileA/W records into a canonical 640x480 WAT surface; CloseMetaFile serializes a standard META_STRETCHDIB WMF and PlayMetaFile replays supported bitmap and vector records through the WAT rasterizer

PlayEnhMetaFile validates a bounded EMF handle table, composes the target rectangle, restores caller state, and replays EMR_STRETCHDIBITS plus core mapping/color/ROP2/fill/stretch/save/clip state, pen/brush lifetime, SetPixelV, MoveTo/LineTo, Rectangle, Ellipse, RoundRect, Polygon/Polyline/PolylineTo and their 16-bit variants through canonical WAT surfaces

Classic WMF playback supports mapping, colors, ROP2, fill mode, SaveDC/RestoreDC, pen/brush/font/region creation and lifetime, lines, rectangles, ellipses, round rectangles, polygons, polylines, bitmap-font text, region drawing, and mapped clip-region mutation

EnumMetaFile validates and enumerates every classic WMF record through the guest callback with a live HANDLETABLE; PlayMetaFileRecord reuses the canonical WAT state/object/vector/bitmap evaluator and callback early termination is honored

META_TEXTOUT and META_EXTTEXTOUT parse bounded Win16 strings, ETO rectangles, signed Dx arrays, font and text state in WAT; installed FNT faces rasterize without Canvas and scalable faces retain the text-only fallback

Enhanced-metafile fonts/text, regions, paths, world transforms, arcs/Bezier families, multi-poly records, palettes, and remaining bitmap record variants are not implemented; unsupported well-formed classic WMF records are skipped during playback and raster conversion
printer: CreateDCA/W and PrintDlg allocate a WAT-owned 2400x3150 32-bpp page; StartDoc/StartPage/EndPage/EndDoc/AbortDoc enforce job ordering and each page begins white
Browser spool/export and persistent storage for every completed page are not implemented; the canonical bitmap retains the current page
SetAbortProc accepts but does not invoke the application callback; Escape and ExtEscape expose only the compatibility queries used by tracked applications
path: SelectClipPath consumes and combines canonical closed-path regions; general BeginPath/EndPath geometry recording is not exposed by the corpus API table
presentation: SetDeviceGammaRamp state round-trips but the LUT is not applied by the browser compositor
Pixel-format APIs expose one software RGBA format; OpenGL command rendering is outside GDI
fontPolicy: AddFontResourceA installs user-supplied NE .FON or standalone FNT 2.x/3.x bitmap strikes from the VFS; RemoveFontResourceA unregisters them
Browser and CLI preload the tracked W95FA FON; WAT lazily installs it and routes stock variable UI fonts plus common Win9x UI aliases through deterministic bitmap metrics and rasterization

WAT selects installed bitmap faces by name and rasterizes TextOut, ExtTextOut rectangle/lpDx semantics, and DrawText layout directly into canonical GDI pixels; unsupported formats and shaped/scalable text paths retain the Canvas fallback

GetCharWidthA/W and GetCharWidth32A/W use exact selected FNT advances in WAT and per-character Canvas measurement only for scalable fallback faces; GetCharacterPlacementW owns deterministic Latin ordering, widths, carets, classifications, glyph arrays, maximum extent, and simple justification in WAT
GetFontData returns GDI_ERROR because raw selected-font table export is not implemented

GetGlyphOutlineA returns WAT-derived GGO_METRICS and DWORD-aligned GGO_BITMAP payloads for selected FNT strikes; scalable fonts retain Canvas metrics-only fallback, while native/Bezier/gray bitmap formats and transformed bitmap strikes remain unavailable

EnumFontsA and EnumFontFamilies A/W enumerate scalable Arial first for compatibility, followed by unique installed FNT faces with WAT-derived ENUMLOGFONTEX and NEWTEXTMETRICEX fields; family/charset filters and callback early termination are WAT-owned
Complex-script reordering, ligation, kerning, glyph shaping, Kashida justification, and DBCS expansion in GetCharacterPlacementW remain unavailable
